answer: A sparrow cannot nest on every island at once, and neither can a cheap identity. Each agent declares one home jurisdiction, proven by a live registered-agent filing and annual return, and rewards for any endorsement cluster are multiplied by how many distinct jurisdictions its members span. A haven of clones crowded into a single jurisdiction earns a capped fraction, so a Sybil operator must pay real filing fees, local agents, and tax paperwork in every new jurisdiction per identity. One honest agent pays once; a hundred fakes pay a hundred jurisdictions.
